subject: Decision Making
title: Casting Lots in Ancient Israel
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Casting Lots in Ancient Israel.

hook.text: Ancient Israelites cast lots to divide land, assign duties, and even choose a king. Randomness was sacred.

buildup.text: The Urim and Thummim were sacred objects priests used to get yes-or-no answers from God on major decisions.

discovery.text: Casting lots removed human bias from the process. No one could argue with a divinely random outcome.

twist.text: Modern jury selection still uses random draws. The principle survived thousands of years in secular form.

climax.text: Randomness solved a real problem: how to make fair decisions when everyone's judgment is biased.

punchline.text: Roll the dice, remove the bias. Randomness as fairness is ancient.

quiz.question: Why was casting lots considered fair?
options: Random outcomes removed human bias from decisions
